title: Console: set zod jitless so the boot does not probe eval
body:
Filing-gate category: ① user-visible defect with a named landing site (follow-up owed by landed work: objectstack#25569). Maintainer approved this follow-up (12d).

Reader who acts: the objectui card thread that takes this; one-line change in the Console boot (`apps/console/src/main.tsx`) plus a test.

Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectui jitless` → 0 hits; `zod eval` → 0 hits.

## Problem

zod v4 decides whether to use its JIT by running `Function('')` once inside a try/catch (`allowsEval`). Under the Console document's content-security-policy (objectstack#25569), `'unsafe-eval'` is absent whenever the react-pages tier is off (`OS_PAGE_REACT=off`), so every document load reports one `script-src` eval refusal. Nothing breaks, but:

- each load sends a CSP violation report, which buries real ones for operators who collect reports;
- once the react-pages tier defaults to off (security order S3), this becomes every deployment.

reach: measured once through the public UI — browser smoke on objectstack#25569's branch with `OS_PAGE_REACT=off`: exactly one eval refusal per document load, traced to zod's `allowsEval` probe in the Console bundle. (Not yet measured with `jitless` set; the card's acceptance check covers that.)

## Proposed change

Call `z.config({ jitless: true })` at the top of the Console boot, before any schema is built. zod then skips the probe and uses its interpreter path. Apply it unconditionally: the JIT gain on the Console's schemas is negligible, and one code path is simpler than switching on the tier.

## Acceptance

- A unit test asserts the Console boot sets `jitless` (or that building and parsing a schema never calls `Function`).
- With `OS_PAGE_REACT=off` and objectstack#25569's policy, a Console load reports no eval violation.

Business rationale: operators who turn on CSP reporting should see only real violations; without this, every page load files a false one.
